findings.evidence: Sibling lemmas exist and are used exactly this way: `le_enlarge` at :221 used in `enlarge_idealOfDefinition` :232; `le_adjoin` at :250 used in `adjoin_idealOfDefinition` :261; `le_sup_left` at :316 used in `sup_idealOfDefinition` :331; `le_sup_right` at :322. `grep -n 'le_enlargeBounded'` in TauCeti/ returns nothing.
findings.fix: Add `le_enlargeBounded : P.ringOfDefinition ≤ (P.enlargeBounded B hB).ringOfDefinition` and `self_le_enlargeBounded : B ≤ (P.enlargeBounded B hB).ringOfDefinition`; state `enlargeBounded_idealOfDefinition` with `Subring.inclusion (P.le_enlargeBounded B hB)` and close `isBounded_iff_exists_ringOfDefinition_ge` with `P.self_le_enlargeBounded B hB`.

findings.fix: Tag `enlargeBounded_idealOfDefinition` with `@[simp]` (matching `enlarge_ringOfDefinition`/`enlargeBounded_ringOfDefinition`, which are both simp).
findings.issue: `enlargeBounded_idealOfDefinition` carries no `@[simp]`, unlike every other `*_idealOfDefinition` lemma in the file. Because `enlargeBounded`'s body is not exposed, `enlarge_idealOfDefinition` cannot fire through it, so no simp lemma computes `(P.enlargeBounded B hB).idealOfDefinition`.

summary: The new `enlargeBounded` surface is missing the two inclusion lemmas every sibling construction in the file provides, which forces an inline `show ... by rw` proof term into the statement of `enlargeBounded_idealOfDefinition` and makes consumers reprove `B ≤ (P.enlargeBounded B hB).ringOfDefinition`. The ideal lemma also lacks the `@[simp]` its three siblings carry.
